headline: Seasonal Beach Tags and Historic Inn Reservations
reservation: Beach access requires the purchase of seasonal, weekly, or daily tags from June through September; check official booths for current rates. Accommodations in historic Victorian inns often book out six to twelve months in advance for peak summer and autumn festival weekends.

days.title: Victorian Heritage
days.start: Suggested: 9:30 AM from Washington Street Mall

stops.name: Emlen Physick Estate
stops.detail: Tour this 1879 Stick Style mansion to understand Victorian-era daily life and architecture.

stops.name: Historic District Painted Ladies
stops.detail: Walk or cycle Hughes Street to see the intricately decorated 19th-century framed buildings.

days.driving: Allow 15 minutes; walking or cycling is highly recommended in the center
days.note: Trolley tours provide historical context but require advance ticket pickup.

days.title: Lighthouses and Diamonds
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Cape May Point State Park

stops.name: Cape May Lighthouse
stops.detail: Climb the 199 steps for views of the confluence of the Delaware Bay and Atlantic Ocean.

stops.name: Sunset Beach
stops.detail: Search for 'Cape May Diamonds' (quartz pebbles) and view the wreckage of the SS Atlantus.

days.driving: Allow 25 minutes; parking at the Point can be limited during birding season
days.note: The climb involves steep spiral stairs; landing platforms are available for rest.

days.title: Nature and Harbor Life
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from South Cape May Meadows

stops.name: South Cape May Meadows
stops.detail: Walk the loop trails through freshwater marshes to spot migratory raptors and shorebirds.

stops.name: Nature Center of Cape May
stops.detail: Explore the educational gardens and observation tower overlooking the busy harbor.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes; watch for heavy bicycle traffic along the harbor roads
days.note: Meadow trails are exposed; carry water and use sun protection even in breeze.

intel.title: Historic District Congestion
intel.text: Metered street parking is strictly enforced and difficult to find during summer; utilize the municipal lot at Congress Hall. Many visitors prefer parking once and using the seasonal trolley or bicycles.

intel.title: Reliable Town Coverage
intel.text: Signal is strong throughout the town and beaches, though it may dip slightly in the dense foliage of the County Park. Public Wi-Fi is available at the Washington Street Mall area.

intel.title: Parkway Access Points
intel.text: Fuel stations are located just north of the canal along Route 109 and the Garden State Parkway. There are no gas stations within the primary historic residential district.

intel.title: Migration Peak
intel.text: Autumn is the busiest time for birdwatching at the Hawk Watch platform; expect large groups of enthusiasts. Check the local count calendars if you wish to see specific migratory peaks.

intel.title: Pedestrian Mall Zone
intel.text: Washington Street Mall is a three-block vehicle-free zone dedicated to pedestrians. Bicycles must be walked in this area during designated hours to ensure safety.

plan.arrival: After pickup at ACY, drive south via the Garden State Parkway. Check into your inn and drop your bags before walking to the Washington Street Mall for orientation.
plan.vehicle: Compact cars are ideal for narrow historic streets; many visitors find bicycles more efficient than driving. Check for local 'BYOB' restaurant policies when planning meals.
plan.goldenHour: Sunset Beach is the premier location for watching the sun drop over the Delaware Bay.
